A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same switchback-experiment study. All 39 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are available and readable; text, equations, figures and proofs support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original linear and nonlinear simulations, ridesharing-data-based simulations, and bootstrap coverage and bias/variance results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v5 retains original synthetic and ridesharing-data-based simulation outcomes, including estimation errors, confidence-interval coverage, biases and standard deviations.

M1.justification: The switchback allocation rules and OLS, LSTD, modified LSTD and DRL estimation procedures are unchanged. Appendix A retains the same implementation algorithms and equations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same linear and nonlinear synthetic environments and two 40-day ridesharing datasets. The covariance structures and carryover-effect scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Figure 5 and Appendix C retain the same external comparators: Bojinov et al. (2023), Hu and Wager (2022), and Xiong et al. (2024). No comparison method is added or replaced.

E3.justification: The stated sample sizes, horizons, simulation procedures and burn-in length remain unchanged. Figure 5's caption changes from log root MSE to log MSE, matching the axis and Appendix C already in v3; this does not establish a metric change.

E4.justification: The covariance-sensitivity tests, bootstrap coverage analysis and synthetic/real-data bias–variance analyses are retained. Figures S4–S5 redisplay the existing analyses without introducing a new ablation or robustness question.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the 200-simulation aggregation and the same bootstrap confidence-interval construction, coverage and width reporting. The redrawn plots introduce no new run counts, seed disclosures or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v5 Figure 5 exposes comparisons by sample size and correlation but omits v3's m=24 and m=48 result summaries, showing only m=1, 3, 6 and 12. Figures S4–S5 also expose individual-setting results previously pooled in boxplots. The principal findings remain consistent.

T1.justification: Appendix D.2 removes Assumption 2, which bounds the OLS-based ATE estimator, from the DRL and LSTD theorem requirements. It remains required for OLS. The bounds, corollaries and proof derivations are otherwise unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that carryover strength and reward-error autocorrelation determine switchback efficiency across several RL estimators. The abstract, introduction and practical design recommendations retain their scope.

C2.justification: The explanations involving error cancellation, distribution shift and model misspecification are retained, as are Appendix B's Markov-assumption limitations. Section 6's expanded temporal-randomization paragraph restates the existing equivalence argument.

D1.justification: The implementation details, simulation coefficients, dataset dates and time intervals, regularization selection, bootstrap instructions and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to A/B testing, off-policy evaluation and experimental-design research are unchanged. The reference list only reflows.

P1.justification: v5 expands and rephrases one temporal-randomization paragraph and standardizes several heading capitalizations. The document structure remains stable. Appendix C introduces an unresolved 'Figure ??' reference where v3 identified Figure 5.

P2.justification: Figure 5 and Figures S4–S5 undergo substantial visual redesign: pooled boxplots become extensive grids of curves against sample size, separated by correlation, switching interval, effect size and environment. Axes, panel organization, captions and occupied space change substantially; other figures are retained.

improvement.justification: The disaggregated plots make dependence on experimental settings easier to assess, and Appendix D removes an OLS-specific prerequisite from the other estimators' theorem statements. These provide limited gains in transparency and precision. The benefits are tempered by denser plots, omitted m=24/48 comparisons in Figure 5 and the new unresolved figure reference; the central scientific evidence remains stable.
